description: High-performance structured logging for .NET 9 and .NET 10. Striped async channel queue, MessageTemplate caching, object pooling, PII masking, correlation ID auto-propagation, per-sink minimum levels, per-category log levels, appsettings.json minimum-level configuration, HTTP context enrichers (RequestId, UserContext), one-line correlation middleware, and built-in ASP.NET Core health check. MEL ILogger<T> compatible — drop-in replacement for Serilog/NLog.
releaseNotes:
v1.1.0 — appsettings.json MinimumLevel configuration
• Added: SinkSharpBuilder.ReadFrom(IConfiguration, sectionName = "SinkSharp") — binds MinimumLevel:Default and MinimumLevel:Override:<category> from appsettings.json (or any IConfiguration source) without a redeploy
• Mixes freely with code-based MinimumLevel()/MinimumLevelFor() — both write into the same category-level dictionary, so whichever call runs later in the fluent chain wins for a given category, MinimumLevel.Override
• An unrecognized level name throws InvalidOperationException at startup, naming the bad section path and the value, with the list of valid level names — a config typo fails fast instead of silently falling back
• Deliberately scoped to MinimumLevel only — sinks, enrichers and sampling stay code-only via the fluent builder; this does not read the standard ASP.NET Core Logging:LogLevel section
• No hot-path impact: ReadFrom() runs once at startup before BuildLogger(), same as any other builder call
• 11 new tests covering Default/Override individually and combined, custom section names, absent-section no-op, both mixing orders, invalid level names, and null-argument guards — 576 tests passing (288 per TFM, net9.0 and net10.0)
See full changelog: https://github.com/SinkSharp/.github/blob/main/profile/CHANGELOG.md

v1.0.11 — Shutdown-drain correctness, queue concurrency fixes, and hardening
• Fixed: capacity is now one shared budget across all stripes — a single global occupancy counter replaces per-stripe occupancy/capacity, so whichever stripe(s) actually receive traffic can use the whole configured budget, even under a burst concentrated onto just a few of them (common under ThreadPool thread growth); verified zero drops across Producers=1/8/32 on both a 2-core CI runner and a 20-core workstation
• Fixed: dropped events now return to the internal object pool for reuse, same as processed events
• Fixed: shutdown now drains the rest of a batch cleanly — ProcessAsync substitutes CancellationToken.None immediately when cancellation already fired, instead of throwing/catching per event
• Fixed: thread-to-stripe assignment changed from ManagedThreadId % stripeCount to round-robin with thread-local caching, spreading threads evenly across stripes while still giving each thread exactly one stripe for the queue's lifetime (preserves per-thread emission ordering)
• Fixed: concurrent throughput improved, especially on low-core machines, by removing the parallel "rescue queue" mirror — confirmed unnecessary (BoundedChannelReader.TryRead is reliable after cancellation); on a 2-core CI runner this took SinkSharp's drop rate at 32 producers from roughly 25% down to under 2%
• Fixed: AsyncLogQueue.DrainAndStopAsync() now delivers every event exactly once, even when shutdown cancellation lands mid-flight — covers both a single-sink pipeline and a multi-sink fan-out, including when a fast sink (e.g. Console) and a slower sink (e.g. a webhook HTTP call) are wired to the same event and the slower one is still in flight when cancellation fires
• LogPipeline.ProcessAsync now awaits each sink's task individually (not Task.WhenAll) and retries, with CancellationToken.None, only the specific sink(s) that were genuinely cut short — never a sink that already completed, fast or slow
• Changed: now multi-targets net10.0 and net9.0 (previously net9.0 only) — .NET 9 reached end of support 2026-11-10; .NET 10 is the current LTS. Multi-targeting keeps this package installable on net9.0 projects while adding a native net10.0 build, since a single-TFM bump would have broken net9.0 consumers outright. All SinkSharp packages, samples, and the benchmark project move together. Note: dotnet run on a sample or the benchmark project now needs -f net10.0 (or -f net9.0) since it's no longer single-targeted
• Changed: on machines with 2 or fewer logical cores, the queue now uses a single stripe, avoiding multi-stripe coordination overhead with no parallelism payoff on that little hardware; no change on 3+ core machines
• Changed: QueueCapacity is now one shared budget across all stripes, not split evenly per stripe — if you were padding QueueCapacity 2-5x for extra headroom, that's no longer necessary
• Added: regression tests covering a fast + slow/cancellable sink pair sharing a fan-out, a single-sink pipeline with an in-flight event, and channel-recovery at shutdown for both critical and non-critical channels — every event reaches every sink exactly once, with no exceptions
• All existing functionality unchanged — safe to upgrade from 1.0.10

See full changelog: https://github.com/SinkSharp/.github/blob/main/profile/CHANGELOG.md

v1.0.9 — v1.1 feature release
• Added: ISampler interface + PercentageSampler — probabilistic drop of Debug/Info/Trace events before enqueue; Warning/Error/Critical always pass through; ~2 ns overhead via Random.Shared
• Added: SinkSharpBuilder.WithSampling() — three overloads: SamplingOptions dict, rate+maxLevel simple, custom ISampler
• Added: SinkSharpBuilder.WithUserContext() and .WithUserContext(claims:[]) — no IHttpContextAccessor argument; accessor resolved from DI; fixes hardcoded sub/name/role ignoring AddSinkSharpUserContext(claims:[]) configuration
• Fixed: SinkSharpEnricherStartupService now delegates to registered UserContextEnricher singleton via per-invocation DirectBag (thread-safe); custom claim types now honoured correctly
• Fixed: SinkSharpBuilderTests parallel test isolation — IDisposable with constructor+Dispose resets static _runtimeLevel
• 240 tests passing
v1.0.8 — Correctness fixes
• Fixed: shared Task[] buffer data race in LogPipeline (2+ sinks) — ArrayPool<Task> per ProcessAsync invocation
• Fixed: sink exception permanently killed drainer stripe — per-sink try/catch, SinkFailureCount counter
• Fixed: pool leak on sink exception — ReturnToPool() moved to outer finally
• Fixed: TotalDropped always 0 — atomic per-stripe occupancy counter replaces unreliable TryWrite return value
• Fixed: critical drainer IndexOutOfRangeException — stripeIdx: -1 sentinel; Error/Critical now drain correctly
• Fixed: shutdown race — state machine (Accepting/Draining/Stopped) via Interlocked.CompareExchange
• Fixed: category prefix filter matched "Microsoft" against "MicrosoftExtra" — dot boundary required
• Added: SinkSharpLogger.ClearCallerCaptures() for test teardown; SinkFailureCount observable counter
• 230 tests passing
v1.0.7 — Bug fixes
• DrainAndStopAsync() waits for all drainer tasks — events no longer lost at shutdown
• Lock contention eliminated from hot path — enricher/capture lists lock-free on read path
v1.0.6 — HTTP context enrichers + runtime level control
• AddSinkSharpRequestId() — stamps RequestId from HttpContext.TraceIdentifier
• AddSinkSharpUserContext() — stamps UserId, UserName, UserRole (authenticated only)
• AddSinkSharpRequestPath() — stamps HttpMethod + RequestPath
• AddSinkSharpElapsedTime() — stamps ElapsedMs; requires app.UseSinkSharp()
• All four require builder.Services.AddHttpContextAccessor()
• SetGlobalLevel() / GetGlobalLevel() — change minimum level at runtime without restart
v1.0.5 — Per-sink level, filtering, middleware
• WriteTo(sink, minLevel) — per-sink minimum level; WithDashboard(out sink, minLevel)
• WithMachineName() — standalone MachineName enricher
• Filter(predicate) — drop events before enqueue, zero allocation for dropped events
• WithEnricher(enricher, when: predicate) — conditional enrichment
• app.UseSinkSharp() — X-Correlation-Id middleware + ElapsedTime stopwatch
v1.0.4 — Bug fixes: DisposeAsync idempotent; phone PII regex corrected for (555) 123-4567 format
v1.0.1 — Bug fix: email PII regex corrected
v1.0.0 — Initial release: striped async channel queue (1 per CPU core), MEL ILogger/ILoggerFactory, object pool, PII masking, CorrelationId enricher
See full changelog: https://github.com/SinkSharp/.github/blob/main/profile/CHANGELOG.md
